item: The WAL starvation soak bounds the log by the time a checkpoint attempt took, counts only a checkpoint the scan could see, and calls a round it could not have failed inconclusive
status: built (draft PR; folded into the shutdown-WAL change)
refs: PR #1475; coordinator 26 Oct 04:21: cause accepted (a fixed byte ceiling standing in for a time bound), fold into the shutdown-WAL PR, relative bound with each term named, the 300 ms fsync delay as the red-without; CI failure on the PR #1466 run (job test, 26 Oct 04:06Z); coordinator 26 Oct 06:39: B3 and M3 of the independent read as the read says, an inconclusive round printed
summary: tests/test_wal_starvation_soak.py failed once on CI (round 2 of 3: 9,261,792 B of WAL against 6 x 1,048,576 = 6,291,456 B) with the code under it unchanged since 18 Oct; the property as the test counted it (10 in-scan releases, a success every round) held in all three rounds, only the ceiling failed. The writer appends 256 KiB every ~20 ms and the size read at the end of the scan is mostly what arrived since the last TRUNCATE finished, which costs 3 to 4 fsyncs (the connections' autocheckpoint, journal_size_limit and the in-scan release reset the log too: with checkpoint_wal stubbed out entirely the log stayed at 1.9 MB): the ceiling was a time bound. Reproduced in this container with strace-injected fsync delay (idle 0 to 796 KiB; 4 and 8 CPU burners did not reproduce; 100 ms gave 1.6 to 2.9 MiB; 300 ms gave 6,394,272 / 6,666,192 / 6,666,192 B with 1 attempt a round, over the old ceiling every round). THE INDEPENDENT READ OF THE FIRST FIX found two things, both reproduced: the new byte bound does not kill the build from before the fix (its scan pins the snapshot, every busy TRUNCATE holds the write lock for its 50 ms busy timeout, the writer slows to 5 to 6.7 MB/s and the log ends at 4.5 to 6.4 MB, inside the bound in 10 of 10 rounds, as it was inside the old ceiling in 9 of 10), and the success assertion counted an attempt recorded after the scan ended, so in the slow regime the original design bug (commit without closing the cursor) passed all four assertions. The test now: allows 6 x the ceiling plus the writer's measured rate x the slowest attempt's part INSIDE the scan (headroom, in_flight and total printed on failure); counts a success only if the checkpoint call was issued after the first chunk was delivered and finished before the scan ended; calls a round inconclusive, printed with its numbers, for the bytes when the allowance reaches every byte the round could have written, and for the property when fewer than four attempts answered inside the scan and none cleared (and skips the test when every round is); runs the build from before the fix and the original design bug as REAL rounds (red when four or more attempts answered; on slow attempts the original bug is inconclusive, no longer a pass); and sets OO_WAL_SIZE_LIMIT_MB through monkeypatch, which a 1 MiB limit leaking into later tests needed. MEASURED on the folded file: the four-mutation scratch check of the accounting (no pin requirement, a post-scan success counted, an unanswered attempt counted, an uncapped extent) is killed by a test each; judging on too few attempts and never calling the bytes inconclusive are killed too; with every fsync delayed the fixed build clears a checkpoint inside the scan in every round up to 60 ms (2 to 8 attempts), in 3 of 4 at 80 ms and in none at 100 ms (0.43 s attempts cannot fit a 0.1 s release window), so the file passes at 50 ms and skips with its numbers at 100 and 300 ms instead of failing. NOT shown: the runner's real fsync latency (nothing logs it); the mechanism reproduces the signature, it is not a measurement of that run. A slow runner now skips this soak, so the property is not exercised there.
